title: Whirlpool of India Ltd - 500238 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Whirlpool of India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11.4% to INR 2,582 crore, a record, but EBITDA margin fell to 4.6% on war-led oil/forex costs and e-waste accounting.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew 11.4% to a record INR 2,582 crore, with management citing record Faridabad output, completed sell-in/sell-out of the new-regulation refrigerator and AC range, and gains in premium categories. Profitability was squeezed: EBITDA was about INR 120 crore at 4.6%, down roughly 377 bps, as oil-linked inputs, a roughly 10% rupee depreciation to 95-96 per dollar, Haryana minimum wage revisions and an e-waste accounting charge were only partly recovered through price. Consolidated revenue rose 12.1% to about INR 2,727 crore with EBITDA at 5.1%. Management guided that July-September will be the weakest quarter and gave no full-year numbers.

financial_highlights.change: +11.4% YoY, highest ever for a quarter

financial_highlights.value: FY25 up 4%, FY26 up 7%, Q1 FY27 up 11%
financial_highlights.change: from declines in Q1 and Q2 FY26
AC receivables collected; 5 of last 8 quarters negative

segments.name: Air conditioners
segments.commentary: Management said AC is about two-thirds of revenue and was the weakest margin category under the new regulations; Q1 AC sales were up about 50% in the company's outlet KPI and AC shipments rose in April-May ahead of the summer.

segments.name: Refrigerators
segments.commentary: Launched the 654-litre Luxuriem side-by-side with triple evaporator and Intelli Crisper, priced against INR 70,000-80,000 competitor side-by-sides; company previously had no presence above 500-600 litres, and Pune plant began shipping in July.

segments.name: Washing machines
segments.commentary: Washer sales grew over 80% in the quarter per management; Dynamix dispenser now on 50% of the range, and 11 kg top-load launched in Juniper Green. Top-load segment described as highly competitive.

segments.name: Kitchen appliances (Elica)
segments.commentary: Elica revenue and profit growth were cited as strong; management said there is no remaining minority stake to buy and the holding sits with Pralhad Bhutada.

guidance_outlook: No full-year FY27 revenue or margin guidance; management said predicting it is 'close to zero' accuracy.
July-September 2026 expected to be the weakest quarter, with margins lower than April-June but not as low as the year-ago period.
Management aims for above 10-20% AC growth over the next two years, pacing growth to avoid channel stock build-up.
Management expects war-related and e-waste headwinds to ease if resolved, with an equitable e-waste solution sought from government.
Company aims for 10% share of top-load washers in time; 12-15 months of new product launches planned.
capex_capacity: Pune plant started production in July 2026, shipping Luxuriem refrigerators, with INR 245 crore invested in the facility (as stated).
Faridabad plant delivered record manufacturing output in Q1 FY27 despite war and heat-wave supply constraints.
Current utilisation of about 70-75% on an annual basis; management said no immediate capex need in the next 6-12 months.
Capex is an ongoing process; management said cash is not a constraint and capital goes to projects with strong ROI.
demand_pricing: Price increases taken in April and May 2026 only partly offset war-led and regulatory cost increases, creating a net under-recovery.
Management said the company led hikes only in April and May and avoids unilateral moves that could cost share, citing 2022 experience.
Competition in top-load washers has intensified; the company lost share in that segment while gaining elsewhere.
Distribution is near 10% share in some regions versus about 3% in smaller ones; not present at Croma, Vijay Sales or Reliance Digital (per analyst question).

qa_highlights.question: Parent refinancing and plans for the remaining stake; the cash on the balance sheet.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the parent, Whirlpool Corporation, holds 39.75% and it does not discuss parent matters. The board is examining capital use across manufacturing expansion, automation and inorganic opportunities, with no decision announced.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year revenue growth and margin expectations, including whether OPM could be flat year on year.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide; it said the outcome depends on war, forex and regulatory developments, and that margin protection is a focus.

qa_highlights.question: Whether industry can pass on further price hikes, and the elasticity of a 10% increase.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price coordination is illegal and that it decides pricing independently; a 5% price move equals about INR 1,000 per unit, and not all cost inflation will be recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the about 400 bps margin compression between war, regulation and P4G actions.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the war impact (oil and forex) was larger than the regulatory impact; P4G savings were largely offset as input-supply constraints limited negotiation leverage, and fixed costs were held flat as a percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Sale of services to the parent (INR 250 crore in FY25) and ESOP vesting terms.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the transitional services agreement runs to 2029 on a cost-plus, arm's-length basis; ESOPs were issued at market value with performance-linked vesting and a 3-year cliff.

risks_watch: Oil-linked input costs (MDI, polyol, EPS, plastics) and rupee at about 95-96 per dollar; about 30% of raw materials imported and several Middle East-sourced items are single-sourced.
E-waste accounting provision: management is seeking an equitable industry solution and said the impact is significant.
July-September weakness in AC, which is about two-thirds of revenue.
Price competition in top-load washers and whether the company can hold share while raising prices.
Parent Whirlpool Corporation at 39.75% stake and undisclosed capital-allocation plans.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and new launches, but cautious on margins; management repeatedly declined to quantify full-year outcomes and attributed the margin squeeze to war, forex and regulation. Evasive on the parent's capital plans and the remaining stake.
key_quotes: Revenue is up 26% and profits are up 22%.
